title: Wiki Brain node
description: Common shape for every node. Layer-specific requirements are applied on top of this by the allOf branches at the end. The layer invariant (a node may cite only strictly-lower layers) is NOT expressible in JSON Schema and is enforced by bin/wb-validate.

id.description: type-prefix:slug. Stable forever — a rename is a new node plus a `supersedes` field, never an edit.

confidence.description: Should reflect evidence quality, not how plausible a model finds the claim.

cites.description: The evidence relation. Strictly-lower layers only.

edges.description: Typed semantic relations, grouped into families by schema/edges.json. Unlike `cites` these make no evidence claim and are not layer-constrained — which is exactly why each must declare its strength, its basis and who asserts it.

importance.description: A mundane event scores high if it explains many later ones.

sensitive.description: Excluded from every published artifact. This repository is public.

testimony.description: L0 only. This source's ASSERTIONS are the evidence, not the things it asserts. Set on material whose reliability is unestablished — a prior system's conclusions, a retrospective account, a third party's summary. Every datum extracted from such a source must carry `attributed_to`, which wb-validate enforces.

measurement.description: L1 only. This datum MEASURES its cited sources as artifacts — counts, sizes, hashes, string searches — rather than relaying anything they assert. Exempts it from the `attributed_to` requirement on testimony sources, because there is no assertion to attribute: the source is the object being measured, not a witness being quoted.

attributed_to.description: L1 only. Whose assertion this claim is. `claim = "P"` with attributed_to = src:X reads as 'X asserted P' and makes no claim that P is so. Required on any datum citing a source marked `testimony`, and must appear in that datum's `cites`.

perspective.description: Self-model, external model and LLM model never silently collapse into one another.

persistence.description: 'socially withdrawn', 'low sociability' and 'avoids people after conflict' are three different claims.

counterexamples.description: A pattern that has never looked for its own counterexamples is an anecdote.

negative.description: Absence is informative, but these three are not equivalent.

supersedes.description: Node identity: this node replaces that one. Not the `displaced` edge, which says the thing described here overtook the thing described there.

falsifiers.description: L3+ only. Specific observations that would break this claim, each concrete enough for someone else to go and look for. A reading that cannot say what would refute it is not a reading, it is a preference.

rechecked.description: When this node was last re-checked against the nodes it cites. Clears a staleness warning even when nothing changed — a re-check that finds nothing is otherwise indistinguishable from nobody looking.

edge.description: Vocabulary and families are defined in schema/edges.json. bin/wb-validate errors if this enum and that file drift apart.

strength.description: How hard the claim is. Absent means unaudited, and wb-validate says so out loud rather than letting it pass as settled.

basis.description: What the edge rests on. Required on the causal family: sequence is not causation, and the schema refuses to let the two be written identically.

asserted_by.description: Who makes this claim. Mirrors `perspective` on interpretations for the same reason — an LLM's inferred edge and a stated one must never be indistinguishable. Required on the narrative family.

causal_basis.description: DEPRECATED alias for `basis`, accepted one release so nothing breaks. wb-validate warns on every use.

when.description: Edges are temporal too. A relation true in 2015 can be false by 2020, and a system that calls personality a trajectory cannot hold its edges frozen.

date.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Precision is meaningful — do not pad.
